Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent

Class ModelEvents<T extends Model>

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.ModelEvents<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the model class
public final class ModelEvents<T extends Model> extends Object
The listener registrar of one model class, reached through ModelQuery.events(). Each registration appends a listener and returns this registrar, so calls chain.

For every event the model's own hook runs first, then the listeners in registration order. Only a false from a listener halts, and only the six halting events (saving, creating, updating, deleting, restoring, force deleting) can be halted; a halted event stops the listeners after it and cancels the operation. A listener that throws propagates its exception to the caller.

Listeners are static per model class and are never removed except by forget(). Register them once at start-up, not per request, or every registration fires.

Listeners belong to the class entry registered with ModelQuery.of(java.lang.Class<T>, java.util.function.Supplier<T>), so they apply to every instance and every derived entry of the class. Registration is thread safe and takes effect for the next event. The mute of withoutEvents is per thread and does not cross to an executor or another thread. A write a listener makes inside saveOrFail joins that transaction only through the saving model's getQueryFactory().

  • Method Details

    • afterCommit

      public ModelEvents<T> afterCommit()
      Returns a view of this registrar whose registrations run after the commit.

      The view shares this registrar's listeners: what it registers is visible through ModelQuery.events() and removed by forget(). Each listener registered through it for saved, created, updated, deleted, softDeleted, restored or forceDeleted runs after the outermost commit of the connection that wrote the model, in registration order, on the thread that committed. Outside a transaction it runs at once; when the transaction or its savepoint rolls back it never runs. The listener sees the model as it is when it runs, not as it was when the event fired.

      A halting event cannot wait for the commit, because its result decides the write that is still to run, and retrieved and replicating are not write events, so the view refuses them. A save, delete, restore or force delete of a class that has such a listener fails with IllegalStateException, before it writes anything, when the model's connection runs in a transaction opened outside this library; bind the model to a connection that owns its transaction instead. Events muted by withoutEvents queue nothing.

      Returns:
      a view that registers after-commit listeners, never null; calling it on the view returns an equivalent view
      API Note:
      Register after-commit listeners once, at start-up, like every other listener. Each deferred callback holds its model until the outermost commit, so a large import that saves many models in one transaction keeps every one of them, once per listener, reachable until then; commit in batches.

    • observe

      public ModelEvents<T> observe(ModelObserver<? super T> observer)
      Registers an observer, one listener that receives every event through the matching method of ModelObserver. It runs in registration order among the other listeners.

      When ModelObserver.afterCommit() returns true, or this is the afterCommit() view, the observer's non-halting write events wait for the commit as afterCommit() describes and its halting methods run in the transaction as usual.

      Parameters:
      observer - the observer, never null
      Returns:
      this registrar
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if observer is null
